$comment: D-ASM-SUB-NATIVE-OPERAND-UNUSABLE-IN-INLINE-ASM: the first runnable witness that a `char` or a `short` can be a GNU extended-asm operand. ★★★ THIS EXAMPLE WAS BORN RED. ✔MEASURED through the real CLI on a clean HEAD build, x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec and x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec at debug AND release: `__asm__("movb %1, %0" : "=r"(r) : "r"(v))` on `char` operands was `error[A0008] unknown mnemonic 'movb' — it is not in this dialect's instruction table`, `movw` the same at width 16, and the `movl`-on-a-char alternative was `error[A0008] 'movl' declares operand width 32, but its register operands are 8 bits`. Every inline-asm example already in the tree binds an `int`/`long`/`long long`, and that was not taste — it was the only thing that worked. ✔THE REFERENCE DISJUNCTION, MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 compiles AND RUNS all twelve shapes at -O0 and -O2 (exit 42), and REFUSES the `movl`-on-a-char spelling exactly as DSS does, so conformance runs both ways. ★★★ THE DEFECT THIS EXAMPLE EXISTS TO CATCH IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHY SHAPES 8 AND 9 LOOK ODD: AT&T `movb (%rax), %cl` is `8A /r` and writes ONLY `cl`, while the target's width-8 `load` row is `0F B6` (MOVZX, which gas spells `movzbl`) and ZEROES the upper bits. Both assemble, both run, and nothing reads the difference unless a bit ABOVE the written field is required to survive — which is what those two shapes do: a zero-extending encoding returns 42 where the correct one returns 298 / 65578. This is why the memory-source direction is a SEPARATE opcode (`load_subreg`) rather than a variant on `load`: one (opcode, operandKinds, width) triple cannot denote two machine instructions, and the schema loader refuses the attempt. ★★ TWELVE SHAPES, EACH ITS OWN EXIT CODE: (1,2) register-to-register byte and word moves; (3) an immediate into a byte register (`C6 /0 ib`, riding the existing 1-byte slot); (4,5) memory SOURCE at 8 and 16 bits, i.e. `load_subreg`; (6,7) memory DESTINATION on a global, so the address is a relocated symbol; (8,9) the zero-extension DISCRIMINATORS; (10,11) an operand whose source register provably holds bits ABOVE its own width; (12) HAND-WRITTEN narrow register spellings (`%ax`, `%dl`), which is what the 16-bit `registers[]` rows exist for — a bound `%N` never needs them because its width comes from `AsmOperandBinding::widthBits`, but `%ax` written in the text does. ★★★ SHAPES 10 AND 11 ARE THE MEASUREMENT OF A LABELLED SUSPECT: `MirToLir::emitAsmOperandMove` emits an operand's materialisation copy at the target's default width (64) regardless of the operand's `widthBits`, and the trigger could not fire while `char`/`short` were refused. ✔MEASURED in the emitted code once it could — `mov %r15,%r15` (REX.W 8B /r) ahead of `mov %r15b,%r15b` — and it is VALUE-CORRECT on this target: a full-register copy preserves the low N bits exactly, and the output capture re-reads at the operand's own width (`movsbq`/`movswq`), so the upper bits never reach a consumer un-recast. These two shapes hold that conclusion by execution rather than by argument. ⛔ NO aarch64 TARGET, AND IT IS A DECISION: a `char` operand is still refused there (that CPU declares no 8/16-bit GPR ALU forms), and whether it should instead substitute the 64-bit `x` view — as gcc and clang do — is `D-ASM-BARE-OPERAND-WIDTH-DIVERGES-FROM-REFERENCE`, an OPERATOR decision whose two arms give OPPOSITE answers for this exact question. Writing either here would be a speculative build. ⚠⚠ THIS SENTENCE SHIPPED FALSE AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE RATHER THAN DELETED, BECAUSE THE SHAPE IS THE REUSABLE PART. It said `movw $imm, %reg` STAYS REFUSED, citing a row a sibling lane closed IN THE SAME COMMIT. The mechanism it named was real: a 16-bit immediate is `66 C7 /0 iw` and the x86-variable encoder used to declare no 2-byte immediate slot, so emitting the 4-byte one would have corrupted the instruction stream silently — which is why it was fail-loud rather than approximated. The slot now exists (`EncodingSlotKind::Imm16Bytes`) and D-ASM-X86-NO-16BIT-IMMEDIATE-SLOT is CLOSED; ✔RE-MEASURED at the CLI, `movw $42` into an `=r` short compiles rc=0 and RUNS at debug and release. Shape 3 still spells the BYTE form because the 1-byte slot is what it exists to test. ⇒ a cross-lane citation of an OPEN row is a claim with an expiry date, and the fold is when it expires (D-COMMENT-A-CLAIM-TRUE-WHEN-TYPED-AND-FALSE-WHEN-THE-COMMIT-LANDED). ⚠ The `volatile` seeds are load-bearing: without them the release pipeline folds the values before lowering and silently changes which mechanism each arm tests.
